free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'You can use Killercoda completely for free!' and 'If you open any scenario then you can use it for one hour max, after which the environment of the scenario is deleted. Then you can reload your browser tab to get a new environment which you can use for one hour.' and 'There are no daily or monthly usage limits.'

per_object_cap.stated: Quoted: 'Open up to 3 scenarios at the same time' is a paid-PLUS feature, so a free account holds one environment at a time

retention.stated: Quoted: 'All environments are ephemeral, isolated from each other, and deleted once the browser tab is closed.' Nothing persists between sessions.

egress.terms: not published: no traffic allowance is stated in the FAQ or the pricing page. The environments are built to run labs, so outbound package installs work, but no figure is given.

interface_detail: A browser terminal into an ephemeral Linux environment, plus a remote desktop for some scenarios. No SSH from outside and no public inbound port for user services.
chaining: A one-hour Linux sandbox with no card, useful for a throwaway shell or a Kubernetes exercise, and too short-lived to be a node.

limits.value: one hour per environment, then it is deleted
the environment is deleted when the browser tab closes
short-term rate limits on how often environments can be started, and a Captcha when many users share an IP
registration required; some email domains are blocked

binding_note: One hour and a tab close is the whole lifetime, which is the shortest useful window after Binder's ten-minute reap.

identity_cost.detail: no card, no phone, no document: 'Users wanting to use your scenarios will just need to register for free on Killercoda.' The FAQ adds 'Are some email domains blocked? Yes, certain email domains are blocked due to security measures', so the email must be from a domain the vendor accepts, and the list is not published.

reliability_note: No reliability event observed. The FAQ names short-term rate limits and Captcha challenges when many users share an IP, which is a capacity control rather than an outage.
confidence_note: The one-hour limit, the tab-close deletion, the absence of daily or monthly caps, the registration requirement and the blocked-domain policy are quoted from Killercoda's own FAQ read. The per-environment vCPU and RAM are not published anywhere read, so no shape is recorded.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'If you open any scenario then you can use it for one hour max, after which the environment of the scenario is deleted. Then you can reload your browser tab to get a new environment which you can use for one hour. This one hour limit is raised to four hours with a paid membership. There are no daily or monthly usage limits.'
quoted: 'All environments are ephemeral, isolated from each other, and deleted once the browser tab is closed.'

quoted: 'To protect the platform there are short-term rate limits, for example on how often you can start environments. And if too many users connect from the same IP address there will be Captcha Bot Detection challenges shown.'
quoted: 'Users wanting to use your scenarios will just need to register for free on Killercoda.' and 'Are some email domains blocked? Yes, certain email domains are blocked due to security measures.'
quoted: 'Use all free scenarios as much as you want (excluding Courses)' under FREE, and 'Use scenarios for up to 4 hours instead of just one' and 'Open up to 3 scenarios at the same time' under PLUS

notes: Free, no card, no phone, and renewable all day because there are no daily caps: the constraint is that each environment dies at one hour or when the tab closes. That makes it a lab bench rather than a host. Two things are unverified: the per-environment shape (no vCPU or RAM figure is published on any page read) and which email domains are blocked. The existing `killercoda` record prices it as a trial at 1 hour with a 4-hour paid tier; this record adds the no-daily-cap statement and the registration detail that the earlier one lacked.

shape.note: not published on the FAQ or the pricing page

extras.price_arithmetic: no charge and no payment field; ten one-hour environments a day cost nothing because there are no daily caps

network_out.ports: browser terminal and remote desktop only; no public port for a user service

session_cap.note: one hour, deleted at tab close, no daily cap

extras.payment_methods: none; the free membership takes no payment
